# Kyoto Trip Plan for Two Adults: 2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13

A comfortable, transit-friendly 4-day Kyoto plan focused on temples, gardens, local food, and one short shopping stop. I’ve kept walking lighter, centered each day around one area, and budgeted for a station-area hotel under **$180/night**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Estimated Costs

### Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and Easy Riverside Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive in Kyoto, check in near **Kyoto Station** or **Gojo Station**; keep the first day light.
- **Afternoon:** Gentle visit to **Kiyomizu-dera area** by taxi or bus, then rest at a café near Gion.
- **Dinner:** Try **yudofu** or **kaiseki-style set lunch/dinner** in Gion or Higashiyama.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel **$160**; local transit/taxi **$20**; food **$95**; admissions/snacks **$20**; total **$295**

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens, Temple Views, and Scenic Lunch
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Take the train to **Arashiyama** early; use taxis or short shuttle rides where possible.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Tenryu-ji Garden** and the **Bamboo Grove** at a relaxed pace; skip extra hills if the knee is sore.
- **Dinner:** Return to central Kyoto for **izakaya small plates** or **soba** near the station.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel **$160**; transit **$18**; food **$100**; admissions **$18**; total **$296**

### Day 3: Northern Kyoto Temples and a Half-Day Shopping Stop
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** and then **Ryoan-ji** by bus/taxi; keep the temple list short and focused.
- **Afternoon:** Half-day shopping at **Kyoto Station Isetan / Porta / Avanti** for souvenirs, snacks, and local crafts.
- **Dinner:** Have **kaisendon**, **ramen**, or **tofu dishes** near Kyoto Station.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel **$160**; transit **$22**; food **$105**; admissions **$16**; shopping allowance **$120**; total **$423**

### Day 4: Nishiki Market, Garden Time, and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Easy breakfast, then **Nishiki Market** for tasting bites and edible souvenirs.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Easy breakfast, then **Nishiki Market** for tasting bites and edible souvenirs, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Choose one low-walk option: **Shosei-en Garden** or a relaxed tea stop; leave time for luggage pickup and station transfer.
- **Dinner:** If departing later, do an early final meal near the station; if leaving midday, use this as a light lunch stop.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel **$160**; transit **$12**; food **$85**; admissions **$10**; total **$267**

## Budget Snapshot and Hotel Fit

| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---:|
| Hotel, 3 nights | $480 |
| Local transit and occasional taxis | $72 |
| Food and drinks | $385 |
| Temple/garden admissions | $64 |
Media: Alt=| Temple/garden admissions | $64 |, Kyoto, Japan
| Shopping allowance | $120 |
| Buffer for extras | $250 |
| **Trip total** | **$1,371** |

**Budget fit:** Well under your **$2,400** cap, leaving room for upgraded meals, a nicer hotel, or extra shopping.

### Best Hotel Area
- **Best base:** Kyoto Station area
- **Why it works:** easiest rail access, fewer transfers, taxis are simple, and it reduces walking for the knee issue
- **Target nightly rate:** **$130–$180**
- **Good nearby station choices:** Kyoto Station, Gojo Station, Karasuma Station

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in April

### Clothing
- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with cushioning
- Easy-on/easy-off shoes for temple visits
- Socks suitable for indoor temple rules
- Small umbrella or compact rain shell

### Knee-Friendly Travel Items
- Compression sleeve or brace if helpful
- Pain relief medication you already use
- Foldable walking stick or trekking pole if normally helpful
- Small seat cushion for trains or long restaurant waits

### Essentials
- Passport and copies of travel documents
- Credit card plus some Japanese yen cash
- Phone charger and power bank
- Universal plug adapter
- Transit app or offline maps
- Compact day bag

### Temple and Food Etiquette
- Easy layers for places where shoes must come off
- Small bag for shoes if needed
- Tissues and hand sanitizer
- Reusable water bottle
